title: Choosing a Mainstream 24-Inch Gaming Monitor: Refresh Rate, Response Time and Ports
excerpt: 24-inch Full HD is still the size eSports players prefer. This guide explains what 144Hz, 180Hz and 1ms really mean and what to check before you buy.

sections.title: Why gamers still choose 24-inch Full HD
sections.content:
At 24 inches, the whole frame fits within your field of view without much eye movement — an advantage in shooters and MOBAs. Full HD (1920×1080) is also light on the graphics card, making high frame rates easier to reach.

If you play RPGs or open-world games and care more about visuals than speed, a 27-inch QHD monitor may suit you better.

sections.title: Refresh rate: how 144Hz, 165Hz and 180Hz differ
sections.content:
Refresh rate is how many times per second the monitor redraws the image. Going from 60Hz to 144Hz is a very noticeable jump: motion is smoother and easier to track. Going from 144Hz to 165Hz or 180Hz is a smaller difference that mostly eSports players will notice.

What matters is that your PC can reach the matching frame rate (FPS). A 180Hz monitor does not help much if your game only runs at 70–80 FPS.

sections.title: 1ms response time: reading the spec correctly
sections.content:
The "1ms" on the box is usually MPRT or measured at the highest overdrive setting, and does not always reflect real-world experience. At overly aggressive overdrive, some monitors show inverse ghosting (overshoot).

When reading reviews, pay attention to comments about blur during fast motion rather than just the number on the spec sheet.

sections.title: Panel type and adaptive sync
sections.content:
Most mainstream gaming monitors today use IPS panels (good color, wide viewing angles) or VA panels (high contrast). Both are fine for gaming; IPS is usually preferred if you both game and work on it.

Adaptive Sync (FreeSync or G-Sync Compatible) reduces screen tearing when FPS fluctuates. It is almost a standard feature, so check for it before you buy.

sections.title: Ports and cables
sections.content:
To run a high refresh rate you need the right port and cable: DisplayPort, or an HDMI version that supports that refresh rate. Some monitors only reach their maximum refresh rate over DisplayPort, so read the manufacturer's specs carefully.

After plugging in, remember to select the correct refresh rate in your operating system's display settings — many PCs default to 60Hz.

faq.question: Does a 144Hz monitor need a powerful graphics card?
faq.answer: It needs to be powerful enough for your games to reach close to 144 FPS at Full HD to get the full benefit. For light eSports titles, a mid-range card is usually enough.

faq.question: Can a laptop output 144Hz to an external monitor?
faq.answer: It depends on the laptop's ports. You need an HDMI or USB-C/DisplayPort port that supports that refresh rate; check the laptop's specs first.

faq.question: Can a gaming monitor be used for office work?
faq.answer: Yes. A 24-inch Full HD IPS monitor works well for office tasks, and the high refresh rate makes scrolling smoother too.
